title: Agency & Partnership
description: Business Associations, Weeks 1–8 (Bainbridge, Park & Rodrigues, 6th ed.). Covers creating an agency, actual and apparent authority, ratification and estoppel, a principal's tort liability, agents' fiduciary duties, choosing an entity, partnership formation under the UPA and RUPA, partners' rights, authority and duties, dissociation and dissolution, loss sharing, buyout agreements, limited partnerships, and LLCs.

Agency_and_Partnership_Condensed_Outline.title: Agency & Partnership Outline
Agency_and_Partnership_Condensed_Outline.description: Condensed exam outline of Weeks 1–8, built from the Class 1–8 slides, the casebook, and the 2026 statutory supplement. Part I covers agency: creating the relationship, contract liability and authority, tort liability, and fiduciary duties. Part II covers business entities: choosing an entity, partnership formation, economic rights and property, management and authority, partners' fiduciary duties, dissociation and dissolution, Kovacik loss sharing, buyout agreements, limited partnerships, and LLCs. Rule and tip boxes throughout, and a card for every case (62 main cases plus slide references and supplemental readings).

Agency_and_Partnership_Bar_Questions.htm.title: Agency & Partnership Bar Questions
Agency_and_Partnership_Bar_Questions.htm.description: 284 bar-style multiple-choice questions covering every rule, case, and slide problem in the Weeks 1–8 outline, across 23 topics: creating an agency, actual, apparent and inherent authority, ratification, estoppel, agents' contract and tort liability, scope of employment, independent contractors, and agents' fiduciary duties; then entity selection, partnership formation, property, management and authority, partners' duties, dissociation and dissolution under the UPA and RUPA, loss sharing, buyouts, limited partnerships, LLPs, and LLCs. Each question sets out new facts, and every answer choice has its own explanation. Variations change one fact to test whether the result changes. Filter by topic, shuffle the questions or answers, retry the ones you missed, and use the coverage map to find the questions for any outline item.

Agency_and_Partnership_Practice_Exams.ht.title: Agency & Partnership Practice Exams
Agency_and_Partnership_Practice_Exams.ht.description: 14 practice exams (210 questions) for the Week 10 exam, written in the format of Professor Richardson's sample exam: 15 five-choice questions each, with six stand-alone questions followed by two shared hypos (Q7–11 and Q12–15), and combination choices such as "B and C", "A, B and C", and "None of the above." Together they cover all 14 sections of the Weeks 1–8 condensed outline, from creating an agency through authority, ratification, estoppel, tort liability, and agents' duties, to partnership formation, property, management, partners' duties, dissociation and dissolution under the UPA and RUPA, Kovacik loss sharing, buyouts, LPs, LLPs, and LLCs. Every choice has its own explanation. Study mode checks each answer as you pick it; Exam mode lets you answer a full exam and then grade it. Filter by exam or outline section, shuffle the questions, and retry the ones you missed.

Agency_and_Partnership_Practice_Exams_II.title: Agency & Partnership Practice Exams II
Agency_and_Partnership_Practice_Exams_II.description: A second set of 14 practice exams (210 new questions) for the Week 10 exam, in the same format as the first: Professor Richardson's sample-exam style, with 15 five-choice questions per exam, six stand-alone questions followed by two shared hypos (Q7–11 and Q12–15), and combination choices such as "B and C", "A, B and C", and "None of the above." Together they cover all 14 sections of the Weeks 1–8 condensed outline, and every choice has its own explanation. Agency_and_Partnership_Concept_Exams.htm.title: Agency & Partnership Concept Exams
Agency_and_Partnership_Concept_Exams.htm.description: 14 concept exams (210 questions) for the Week 10 exam, in the format of Professor Richardson's sample exam (15 five-choice questions each, with combination choices such as "B and C" and "None of the above"), but built around the rules rather than long fact patterns. The questions test the fine distinctions: the UPA (1914) against the RUPA on entity versus aggregate theory, property, liability, dissolution, and buyouts; general partnerships against LLPs, LPs, LLLPs, and LLCs on filing, control, liability, agency, and exit; the Restatement (Second) against the Restatement (Third); and which defaults a partnership or operating agreement can and cannot change. Questions 1–6 stand alone, and Questions 7–11 and 12–15 share a focus note naming the topic and statute, such as UPA dissolution, RUPA Article 7 buyouts, LLP shields, or managing an LLC. Every choice has its own explanation, and the exams cover all 14 sections of the Weeks 1–8 condensed outline. Study mode checks each answer as you pick it; Exam mode lets you answer a full exam and then grade it. Filter by exam or outline section, shuffle the questions, and retry the ones you missed.

Agency_and_Partnership_Playlist.title: Agency & Partnership Playlist
Agency_and_Partnership_Playlist.description: Study songs that walk through the Weeks 1–8 outline, one topic per track, numbered to match the planned 17-track album. So far: dissociation versus dissolution, winding up and buyouts, Kovacik loss sharing and buyout agreements, and limited partnerships, LLCs, and veil piercing. Pick any track from the list, or let it play through, at 0.5×, 0.75×, normal, 1.25×, or 1.5× speed.

14_Power_to_Leave.mp3.title: Power to Leave
14_Power_to_Leave.mp3.description: At-will versus term partnerships, and a partner's power to leave versus the right to. UPA automatic dissolution against the RUPA § 603 buyout path, and judicial expulsion. Cases: Collins v. Lewis, Giles, and Page v. Page.

15_Winding_Up.mp3.title: Winding Up
15_Winding_Up.mp3.topic: Outline §10 · Liquidation, buyouts and lingering authority
15_Winding_Up.mp3.description: Statements of dissociation that cut off lingering liability after 90 days, § 701 buyouts at the greater of liquidation or going-concern value, and no forced fire sale. Cases: Creel v. Lilly, Monin v. Monin, and Pav-Saver.

16_Money_vs_Sweat.mp3.title: Money vs. Sweat
16_Money_vs_Sweat.mp3.topic: Outline §11–12 · Loss sharing and buyout agreements
16_Money_vs_Sweat.mp3.description: The Kovacik v. Reed exception, where the money partner bears the cash losses and the service partner loses only their labor, why RUPA rejects it, and the traps in buyout agreements (G & S Investments v. Belman).

17_Welcome_to_the_Fortress.mp3.title: Welcome to the Fortress
17_Welcome_to_the_Fortress.mp3.topic: Outline §13–14 · LPs, LLCs and veil piercing
17_Welcome_to_the_Fortress.mp3.description: General partners' unlimited liability against the LP, LLP and LLC shields; the corporate general partner in Frigidaire v. Union Properties; LLCs as creatures of contract under the ULLCA, member-managed and manager-managed; and veil piercing as the only way through the shield.
